=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py:110-121, 153-156 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A subsequent sync run rebuilds and force-pushes the shared branch using only files changed in that push, dropping earlier unresolved drift fixes from the open sync PR.
  WHY: The missing earlier live-copy fixes remain absent from main and the refreshed PR, leaving parity failures until the drift is synced again.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py:124-126, 156-178 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A failing GitHub API call after the sync branch is force-pushed aborts the script before the PR is opened or updated.
  WHY: The remote branch can be left without a PR pointing to it; severity differs across reviewers, and the highest severity is used.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py:158 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The open-PR query interpolates the raw branch name into the `head` query parameter without URL-encoding.
  WHY: If the HTTP stack encodes slashes or other special characters differently, the lookup may miss an existing PR and lead to a duplicate.
- .github/workflows/sync-claude-live-copies.yml:17-18, 36 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The workflow declares `contents: read` while using `GH_PAT` for write operations, so the declared permissions do not show the workflow's effective write capability.
  WHY: This makes the workflow's write capability harder to audit; qwen_qwen3_7-plus disagrees that this is a capability gap because `GH_PAT` is not governed by the `permissions` block, and the highest severity is used.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py:139-141 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `SYNC_BRANCH` is not validated against `BASE_BRANCH` or protected branches before the script force-pushes to it.
  WHY: Setting `SYNC_BRANCH` to `main` can rewrite the default branch before the subsequent PR creation is rejected; severity differs across reviewers, and the highest severity is used.
- .github/workflows/sync-claude-live-copies.yml:27-46 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The automatic sync workflow has no repository-variable kill switch or invocation gate.
  WHY: Operators cannot pause the workflow during maintenance or a release freeze without modifying or disabling the workflow file.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py:95-97, 147 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: A failed git push raises `CalledProcessError` without emitting a structured `CLAUDE_LIVE_SYNC` log line.
  WHY: Operators must inspect the traceback to distinguish a push failure from a later API failure.
- .github/workflows/sync-claude-live-copies.yml:21 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `cancel-in-progress: false` allows overlapping workflow runs to force-push the shared branch and race between checking for an open PR and creating one.
  WHY: Overlapping runs can create duplicate sync PRs or leave a PR pointing at a stale branch tip.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py:95-97, 147 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `load_divergent` accepts empty or whitespace-only values in the divergence mapping.
  WHY: A blank allowlist reason can cause a file to be excluded from parity checks without a production-side signal.
- .github/workflows/sync-claude-live-copies.yml:27-46 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The sync step performs a commit, force-push, and PR API call without an output gate or a dry-run default.
  WHY: The workflow has no way to inspect or skip the script's write side effects except by removing the step.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:267-270 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The redirection parser removes any final token ending in a digit as if it were a file descriptor.
  WHY: For `git push origin HEAD:feature2 >/dev/null`, it removes the `HEAD:feature2` refspec and may check the current branch instead of the pushed destination.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:328-333 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The `|| exit` shortcut preserves `conditional_cd`, so the following semicolon resets the tracked working directory.
  WHY: A push that runs only after `cd` succeeds may be checked against the session checkout instead of the worktree.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py:131-134, 158-178 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: A push failure raises `CalledProcessError` without a structured log line explaining that the push failed.
  WHY: Operators must read the traceback to determine whether the push itself failed or a later API call did.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "When the push changed a template but not its live copy, it copies the template over and pushes `ai/sync-claude-live-copies`. It then opens a PR, or refreshes the open one."
  expected_change_site: `scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py::sync`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `sync` performs `git checkout -B branch` from current HEAD instead of checking out the existing remote sync branch tip and merging / amending the new files in; combined with the `plan` filter that excludes files not in the current push's `changed` set, the force-push drops any prior drift fixes the open PR carried. There is no test exercising the multi-push accumulation scenario (`tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py::test_sync_pushes_a_branch_and_opens_one_pr` only exercises a single push).
- requirement: "It fails open: with no usable `before` commit it syncs nothing, and the parity test still reports the drift."
  expected_change_site: `scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py::sync` — the force-push + `_gh_json` POST path
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: when the force-push succeeds but the subsequent `gh api` POST raises (transient 5xx, rate-limit), the script aborts with a Python traceback rather than logging `CLAUDE_LIVE_SYNC error reason=api_failed` and exiting 0; the parity test does not run because the workflow step has already failed, so the drift is not reported on this push either. The "parity test still reports the drift" claim holds only when the failure happens before any side effect.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py: lines 110-156 (sync function: plan + checkout-reset + commit + force-push) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The sync function calls plan() to identify only the mismatched files touched in the current push range, then resets the sync branch with checkout -B (dropping any prior commits), commits only the current paths, and force-pushes. When a first push opens a sync PR for files {A,B} and a second push for file C arrives before that PR merges, the branch is reset and only C remains on it. The open PR — or a new one — now describes only C, dropping A and B from the commit history and PR description.
  WHY: If the operator merges the sync PR after multiple pushes without reviewing the actual live copy state, they merge a branch missing earlier synced changes. The branch content no longer matches what the PR was opened for originally. The live copy itself is already synced (plan() only picks mismatched files), so no live-copy data loss occurs, but the sync PR becomes misleading and the commit history on the sync branch is lost.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py: lines 124-126 (_gh_json) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _gh_json uses subprocess.run with check=True and no retry, backoff, or timeout. A transient GitHub API failure (5xx, rate-limit, connection reset) after the git push at line 156 has already succeeded crashes the script — the branch carries the new commits but the PR is never opened or updated.
  WHY: The sync push succeeds, the live copy is updated, but the open-PR GET or PR-creation POST fails. The workflow step exits non-zero and the operator has no PR pointing at the sync branch. The next push to main retriggers the workflow, which reconnects the branch to a PR, so the system self-recovers on a subsequent push. No permanent data loss, but each transient failure leaves one push-cycle gap without a PR.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py: line 158 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The open-PR query URL uses the raw branch name in the head query parameter without URL-encoding. The default branch name ai/sync-claude-live-copies contains forward slashes, which are valid in query-parameter values but could be misinterpreted by intermediate proxies or HTTP clients that percent-encode slashes differently.
  WHY: If any layer in the HTTP stack percent-encodes / in the query value, the API would return no results for a branch that actually exists, causing a duplicate PR to be created. gh's REST transport passes the value literally today, but this is a latent fragility.
- .github/workflows/sync-claude-live-copies.yml: lines 17-18 (permissions: contents: read) vs line 36 (token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The workflow declares contents: read at the top level, but actions/checkout@v5 receives token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }} which grants write access. The git push and gh api calls at lines 39-46 also use GH_TOKEN=${{ secrets.GH_PAT }} for write operations. An operator or automated audit parsing the permissions block would conclude the workflow cannot push commits or open PRs, when in fact it does both on every run.
  WHY: This is a declared-vs-effective capability gap. It does not cause a runtime failure — the GH_PAT token grants the needed write access regardless of the top-level permissions declaration — but it violates the principle of least-privilege declaration and misleads security review of the repository's workflow surface.
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py: lines 139-141 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The script reads SYNC_BRANCH and BASE_BRANCH from the environment with defaults ai/sync-claude-live-copies and main. No validation prevents a malicious or misconfigured SYNC_BRANCH from equaling main or another protected branch. If SYNC_BRANCH were set to main, checkout -B main would hard-reset main to the push's parent commit and force-push it, rewriting the default branch.
  WHY: No sanitization or guard exists before the branch name is passed to git checkout -B and git push --force. The workflow YAML does not expose SYNC_BRANCH as an input or env var, so it defaults safely, but a future operator or automation that injects SYNC_BRANCH could cause catastrophic branch overwrite.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py: lines 110-121, 153-161 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Refreshing an existing open sync PR drops previously staged template drift when a subsequent push to main modifies different template files. plan(root, before, after) computes paths strictly from the files changed between before and after in the triggering push. In sync(), git checkout -B branch resets the local sync branch to after (main) and stages only the latest paths before force-pushing to origin.
  WHY: The template files synced from the earlier push have not yet merged into main, so main still carries the stale live copies.
